intro: Climb the slope where Eskişehir began, and you enter Odunpazarı Houses, a historic town of the 18th–19th century in Eskişehir province. This is the Ottoman quarter: timber houses corbelled out over narrow lanes, and inside them the city's meerschaum carvers still at work.
history: The quarter on the slope where Eskişehir began takes its name from the firewood market once held here. Look up at its timber-framed houses of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries: they corbel out over the lane, each upper floor wider than the one below. And the meerschaum seams of the region made this quarter the centre of the pipe and carving workshops.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the bow-fronted timber houses and the Kurşunlu Complex, then the meerschaum workshops and the Atlıhan.
facts: Did you know? Meerschaum is mined in only a few places on earth, and the finest comes from Eskişehir. It is carved while still soft from the ground, then hardens as it dries. Notice too that the upper floors are wider than the lower ones: the bays corbel out over the lane and win extra rooms from a narrow plot. And the quarter is home to the pipe and carving workshops fed by the Eskişehir seams, which produce the finest meerschaum in the world.
outro: This brings our stroll through Odunpazarı Houses to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These lanes are still lived in and worked in; walk them gently. Enjoy your visit.
